Follow GOAL on Google [...] Cameroon host Namibia in Africa Cup of Nations qualification, with both sides carrying contrasting momentum into what shapes up as a pivotal group fixture.

David Pagou's Cameroon side sit top of Group G and arrive in good form, having beaten Ivory Coast 1-0 in a friendly before the international break following a mixed qualification run that included a draw with Congo and a win over Comoros. [...] The Brave Warriors have shown they can grind out results when it matters. Their 1-0 win over Congo in September demonstrated that quality, even if defeats to Comoros and Kazakhstan in friendlies earlier in the year exposed some vulnerabilities.

Cameroon have their own reasons for caution. This fixture carries real weight in the context of the group standings, and Namibia have proven in recent meetings that they are not here simply to make up the numbers.

One notable omission is attacking midfielder Petrus Shitembi, who sustained an injury while playing for his club.

Namibia is currently third in Group G of the AFCON qualifiers with three points from two matches, one point behind leader Cameroon. Comoros ranks second and Congo tails the group table. ■

Namibia names 22-player squad for AFCON qualifiers against Cameroon [...] Namibia will travel to Douala for the first leg on November 12 before hosting Cameroon in the return fixture on November 16 in Botswana.

Benjamin said the squad combines experienced players with emerging talent, with established internationals expected to provide leadership while younger players get the chance to make their mark.

# USMNT's Mauricio Pochettino, Manchester United Reportedly Finalizing Contract amid Carrick Rumors

While Michael Carrick technically remains the manager at Manchester United, the club have already identified his successor.

David Ornstein of The Athletic reported the club is finalizing a contract with United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino if the decision is made to part ways with Carrick. [...] Having Pochettino leave three months after giving him an extension would be less than ideal for U.S. Soccer. Ripping the bandage off now might be better than the alternative, though.

Even if he stays, this is something that could hang over the national team over the next few years. If he decides to accept a club position at a later point, that's less time for a new coach to execute their plan for the World Cup.

Manchester United hiring Pochettino would carry risk for both sides. [...] Given how far removed he is from his Tottenham peak, an underwhelming tenure at Manchester United could make it difficult for Pochettino to parachute into another major club.
